Record 0: The value-format criterion for the product owner is written in code terms ('dword:', 'hex(n)', 'column 78', trailing backslash, hex bytes) that a person who never saw the code could not follow, and it packs several rules' worth of detail into one sentence.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey One request
disputes: Record 0: The second and third criteria (the success and failure messages) have no cited rule and give no reason, although businessrule-57982804566984189207 states both messages, so they should cite that rule.

Record 0: The term "Policy file" adds "not a registry export file" and the "what" adds "whatever holds it", neither of which the cited rule or the step states as a rule, so they risk inventing behaviour.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Load without questions
disputes: Record 0: Criteria 2 and 3 (domain folder selectable only when joined and the folder exists) and criterion 9 (missing typed folder refused with the exact message, dialog stays open) restate sentences of businessrule-76226373219464614800 and businessrule-53176229115945924012 but cite nothing, so their source is lost.

Record 0: Criterion 4 ("no domain can be reached ... shown as a normal case and the other choices still work") cites integrations.decision-7, a decision about how the API resolves accounts; no rule or decision states that the screen shows this, so it invents behaviour, and "shown as a normal case" is not wording a product owner can test.

Record 0: Criterion 7 (Browse picks a folder and it appears in the folder box) cites integrations.decision-1, which only says the local API reads folders instead of browser pickers and says nothing of a Browse dialog; the behaviour comes from an action with no rule, so the criterion should say it has no cited rule or cite the action's rule, not a decision that cannot carry it.
Record 0: The "what" says the person is told "at once" if the folder does not exist, but the rule only refuses the folder when OK is pressed; nothing states an immediate check.

Record 1: Criterion 1 (nothing loaded, so the person is not asked whether to replace, and the folder loads) cites businessrule-43765682097437166867, which only says the clear-workspace option is ticked by default and passed on when a folder was accepted; the not-asking behaviour comes from the journey step, not that rule, so the citation overstates it.

Record 1: Criteria 2, 3, 5, 6, 8 and 11 (replace proposed by default and add possible, no choice passed on when nothing accepted, adding joins the loaded set, problems reported and load carries on, workspace shows what was loaded and view rebuilt, remembered folder unchanged when adding) are sentences of businessrule-43765682097437166867, businessrule-06850078746756456273, businessrule-19671296259932138006 and businessrule-56221298079625729644 but cite nothing.

Record 1: Criterion 10 (replace chosen, no failure, so the folder is loaded again at the next start) cites integrations.decision-4, which only moves remembered choices to the Preference store, instead of businessrule-56221298079625729644 that states the remembering rule; the decision cannot carry it, and the rule says the folder is remembered, not that it is loaded at start.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Add several at once
disputes: Record 0: Criteria 1, 3 and 4 restate what businessrule-07200475892676201466 decides (ADMX files only, workspace not emptied, not remembered as the definitions folder) yet cite no rule, so only the failure-message criterion traces to it.

Record 0: Criterion 4 invents a timing ("when the program next starts or reloads definitions") that the rule does not state; the rule says only that the file is not remembered as the definitions folder.

Record 0: Criterion 6 says the other files are still added when some are refused, which no cited rule or step states (the steps say only that each file is added alone and each refusal is reported with its reason), and it is also left open whether failures are shown together.

Record 0: Criterion 1 and 2 cover several files, a change the journey step marks merged/inferred, but no criterion says this extends the single-file rule, and the used rule businessrule-61344191921921935952 (adds that file alone, builds the structures) is not reflected in any criterion.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Clear with a way back
disputes: Record 0: Criterion 2 (the view is rebuilt and shows no loaded definitions) restates the second half of businessrule-83939170310206178732 (empties at once and rebuilds the view) but cites nothing, while criterion 1 drops that rebuild; its 'shows no loaded definitions' is also stated by no rule.

Record 0: Criteria 4 and 5 (says what was removed, undo loads the removed definitions again 'as they were') cite no rule and do not say in the criteria that they are new behaviour from the plan with no legacy rule; 'as they were' and what is reported are unstated by any rule or decision, and the open questions show even the scope of undo is undecided.

Record 0: Criterion 3 (closing or replacing the workspace discards definitions and previous search results) is the rule of Session discarder but is a different trigger than the story's clear action and title, and the story's term list defines only 'Loaded definitions' while 'workspace' and 'search results' are used undefined for a product owner.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Contribution at a glance
disputes: Record 0: Five of six criteria cite no rule and the story never says why: the empty-list case ("nothing fails"), the "return to the list" and "other files and list stay unchanged" behaviour state no rule or decision, so they are invented, and the name/folder/namespace columns and counts rest on nothing cited.

Record 0: The fifth criterion ("nothing defined only by the other file appears") only restates the fourth criterion and the cited rule's "only ... defined in that file", so it adds no behaviour, and the story as a whole is close to a restatement of its title with one rule behind it.

Record 0: The open question asks what happens with no file chosen, yet the third criterion states unconditionally that choosing a file opens its details and the legacy rule BR-61081361 (double-click does not check a selection, Enter does) is not reflected or cited, so the criteria and the open point do not agree.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey One place to explore
disputes: Record 0: Every criterion cites only the web layer, yet the story cites no rule and its criteria never say why (the area and empty-category rules sit with the Category tree presenter, which another story builds), and the 'start with everything shown' reason plus the 'empty categories are hidden' precondition state a default that no rule or decision gives.

Record 1: Criteria 2, 3, 5, 7, 10 and 11 restate sentences of the rules for the Item description pane (the Up row, the listing order, the 'selected category' count line, the preference notice, highlighting a category) but cite layer-web instead of those rules, and criterion 1 cites the listing rule for 'becomes the current one and no policy stays chosen', which that rule does not say (it comes from the tree's selection rule).
Record 1: Criterion 9 adds that the policy description is shown on highlighting; the rule only says the policy becomes the selected policy and any highlighted category is cleared.

Record 2: Criteria 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8 and 10 restate the opening, right-click and menu rules but cite layer-web instead of the Item action resolver rules they come from, so the cited rules appear to cover only three criteria; the 'why' also promises that a missing choice never causes a failure while the legacy rule fails with an error and only an open question handles it.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Review then merge
disputes: Record 0: Criteria 2 to 5 state the pairing conditions of businessrule-40351382289100643848 (same name, alone in category, one user and one computer, same explanation and registry key) but cite no rule and give no reason, so they read as invented behaviour.

Record 0: Criteria 1 and 6 (list for review before removal; declining changes nothing) come from the journey's confirm step, not from any rule (the legacy code merges at once with no review), yet the criteria do not say they are a new design decision rather than a rule.
Record 0: Criterion 9 (categories and policy information show the merged policies) is behaviour no cited rule or decision states, and it has no cited rule or stated reason.

Record 0: Criterion 7 says 'the first policy of each pair is removed and the second becomes a policy for both sections', but 'first' and 'second' mean nothing to a product owner who has not seen the code; the criterion should say which policy is kept in words they can follow.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Everything at a glance
disputes: Record 0: The criterion for a policy that names no support definition says the support-details button is disabled, but rule businessrule-59317523370985833904 only says the text is blank for no code (the button is disabled only when the named definition does not exist), and the story's own open question admits the rules do not say; this invents behaviour and contradicts the open item.

Record 0: Seven criteria (computer-only and user-only section, orphaned category, uncategorized, missing support, no support, and the two details-button criteria) have empty 'from' although the first five restate parts of cited rules businessrule-89677004946923202726, 30888155476627040275 and 59317523370985833904, and the last two cite no rule and say nothing about why, so the criteria neither trace to their rules nor explain the absence.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Whole ancestry at once
disputes: Record 0: Criteria 2 and 3 (orphaned parent with disabled button, top-level shows nothing) state exactly what businessrule-88550832449331267612 says but cite no rule (from is empty) and give no reason, so the rule's other two conditions are left uncited.

Record 0: The story promises to reach any parent 'at any level, without climbing one step at a time' and to show the policies the category holds, yet criterion 4 has the person climb one parent at a time and no criterion or cited rule states the policies list or an at-once ancestry chain, so the title/what/why claim behaviour no rule or action states.

Record 0: Criterion 4 ('keep going up until a top-level category or a missing parent is reached') and the 'from a policy in it' opening path are only partly carried by the action blocks and rule, and with from empty and no stated reason it reads as invented behaviour.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Product family in one view
disputes: Record 0: The story promises reading a parent's details in place (action block-94974939167069133577), yet the parent criterion only states the name and the button's enabled state, so what choosing the parent does is never stated as a criterion; and the criterion on double-click or Enter adds 'its details are shown', which its cited rule (only the nothing-selected case) does not say.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Start from the product
disputes: Record 0: The second and third criteria (open on double-click or Enter, nothing happens when nothing is chosen) cite no rule and do not say in their wording that they come from the screen's actions rather than a stated rule.

Record 0: The why and journey step 1 promise finding support rules by the product a person cares about, but no cited rule or criterion filters or lists rules by product coverage, only by name, so that promise is not backed by any rule.

jobs.title: Write the stories of the journey Plain words first, detail on demand
disputes: Record 0: The criterion about a stored comment appearing in the section has an empty citation and gives no reason, although businessrule-77000026808397550095 states exactly that (comment included only when one is stored), so it should cite it.

Record 0: The last criterion joins two unrelated behaviours (comment escaping of backslashes and line breaks, and copying a selected line with Ctrl+C) with 'Also:', so a tester cannot pass or fail each alone; each belongs in its own criterion.

Record 0: The option-value criterion drops parts of businessrule-10913365400690794412: text is written with no escaping so text holding a quote or line break cannot be read back, and quotes inside list-of-text items are doubled.

Record 0: The comment-escaping criterion drops the consequence stated in businessrule-78281155676242942940 (a lone line feed or carriage return splits the comment over two script lines and corrupts it when read back), which is the point of the rule.

Record 0: The criterion on choice names ('named as the file that defines the policy names it') is hard for a product owner to follow; it should say that choice names come from the definitions file that defines the policy.
